topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the course context, and outlines the learning objectives regarding environmental exposures and cancer development.

topics.label: Cancer etiology and the balance between intrinsic and environmental risks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis of cancer as a genetic and evolutionary disease, examining the debate and epidemiological evidence regarding intrinsic bad luck versus environmental exposures.

topics.label: Infectious agents and oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological pathogens contribute to cancer development, highlighting Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Direct and metabolically activated physical and chemical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms by which chemical carcinogens and radiation cause DNA adducts and mutations, often through endogenous metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumour promoters, chronic inflammation, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic factors that facilitate cancer development, focusing on promotional stimuli, chronic inflammation, and developmental or tissue-specific susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and assessing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro techniques used to prove carcinogenicity and determine mutagenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Conclusion and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a summary of environmental cancer causation and reflections on balancing carcinogenic risk against practical benefits.
